# Reproducible dependencies

**libvpx 1.15.2 (VP9 encoder and decoder).** `bash Scripts/prepare-libvpx.sh` downloads the GitHub release tag, verifies SHA256 `26fcd3db88045dee380e581862a6ef106f49b74b6396ee95c2993a260b4636aa`, and builds VP9 only (real-time, no examples/tools/tests) inside `.build/libvpx`. Targets: iPhone arm64 (NEON), simulator arm64/x86_64 (portable C) and macOS arm64 (tests). It installs the ignored `Vendor/VPX.xcframework`. Android sends and accepts only VP9/AV1, and iPhones have no hardware encoder for either. The BSD license (`LIBVPX-LICENSE`) and the patent grant (`LIBVPX-PATENTS`) are retained here.

The current Xcode project links reference **libopus 1.6.1**. Generated binaries are ignored, and no device recordings are retained. Run `bash Scripts/prepare-opus.sh` on a fresh checkout before building this project. The script verifies official-source SHA256 `6ffcb593207be92584df15b32466ed64bbec99109f007c82205f0194572411a1`, builds arm64 iOS 16 and arm64/x86_64 simulator static libraries, creates `Opus.xcframework`, and regenerates the project. It disables optional neural/assembly/runtime-dispatch features for this conservative initial build. The upstream BSD license (`OPUS-COPYING`) and README (`OPUS-README`) are retained here. [Official downloads](https://opus-codec.org/downloads/) and [license](https://opus-codec.org/license/).

The actual bridge uses VOIP mode, mono 48 kHz, 960 samples/20 ms, 20 kbps CBR and complexity 5. Enabled device/simulator compile/link passed. `bash Scripts/diagnose-opus.sh` builds the same pinned source for macOS and checks 100 generated-tone packets, encoded bitrate, decoded sample counts/frequency/power, PLC and state reset; bridge ASan/UBSan is enabled, the upstream library itself is not sanitizer-instrumented. Physical iPhone microphone/playout/radio capacity remain separate checks. If the project is explicitly regenerated without Opus, the bridge uses its unavailable stub and offers only an honest high-bandwidth PCM diagnostic.

The optional **JVM v1 protocol reference** uses Bouncy Castle `bcprov-jdk18on:1.86` lightweight X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, never a global registered provider. Upstream MIT license is retained in `BOUNCY-CASTLE-LICENSE.html`. JUnit 4.13.2, Hamcrest 1.3 and JSON-java 20250517 are test-only dependencies; the script verifies pinned SHA256 values. JUnit/Hamcrest licenses are embedded in their downloaded archives; JSON-java's upstream license is retained in `JSON-JAVA-LICENSE.txt`. `Scripts/setup-interop.sh` installs these locally and optionally Temurin JDK 17.0.20.1+1 for Apple silicon if JAVA_HOME is absent. No system Java/PATH or existing Android installation is replaced. The earlier tool bootstrap also left an ignored SDK/NDK/Gradle cache under `.build/android-tools`; no Android app was created or installed. It may be reused by the Android owner or removed as disposable task output.

`NOISE-C-COPYING` retains the independent Noise known-answer-vector license. Primitive and vector checks do not constitute an independent audit of this application's secure session. Fixture keys and diagnostic peer harnesses are test-only and must never be used as production identities.
